newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies end higher after choppy day.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies end higher after choppy day.

text.p: CME pork belly futures rallied again late to close higher, capping a choppy day that saw August surge to a new contract high and prices also tumble for net losses, traders said. Hog futures closed mostly lower, weighed down by weaker cash hog indications, they said.

Pork belly futures closed 0.750 to 2.000 cents per lb higher with July up 0.800 at 94.150 cents. August posted a new contract high early of 93.850 cents and July came within 0.200 of its previous high.
Hog futures ended 0.650 cent per lb lower to 0.200 higher with June off 0.375 at 81.375 cents.

Locals jockeyed for position after the early runup on technical and fundamental demand failed to boost values to a new contract high in July. Profit taking and local liquidation then pushed prices down into sell stops and prices fell for net losses before trade became even choppier, traders said.

Carryover from Wednesday's sharp gains, following a bullish USDA Cold Storage report on Tuesday, lacked follow through when July failed to post a new high and profit taking developed. This prompted locals to liquidate and trading turned choppy from there. The late rally came on local and commission house short covering, they said.
Prudential Securities sold at the high after early buying by R.J. O'Brien. Also, E.D.&F. Man bought on the later rallies, pit sources said.

Hog futures followed action in bellies early but remained pressured late as expectations increased that cash hog prices would be under pressure until the middle of next week. Packers will need fewer hogs due to the holiday weekend and may not need to purchase many more until Wednesday or Thursday next week. By then, they will be gearing up for a large Saturday kill that usually follows reduced holiday-week slaughter, they said.

Trade was also choppy in hogs late with E.D.&F. Man selling June after buying early. Rosenthal Collins bought late with locals after selling early. R.J. O'Brien was on both sides of the market late, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission houses were on both sides of June 81 puts and 84 calls. FIMAT Futures USA bought July 84 calls. RBH sold June 80 puts, pit sources added.
